title: Center a Box - Three Ways
statement:
Three stage areas (`.a`, `.b`, `.c`) each contain a small `.box`. Center the box **horizontally and vertically** inside its stage using a different technique each time:

1. `.a` - **Flexbox**
2. `.b` - **CSS Grid**
3. `.c` - **Absolute positioning** with `transform`

Do not change the HTML or the stage sizes.

starter.html:
flex
grid
abs

solution.html:
flex
grid
abs

solutionExplanation:
**Flexbox** and **Grid** center children from the parent. The **absolute** technique places the top-left corner of the child at 50%/50% and then pulls it back by half of its own size with `translate(-50%, -50%)`.

All three are O(1) CSS rules; Grid's `place-items: center` is the shortest.
hints: Flexbox: `display: flex` plus `justify-content` and `align-items` on the parent.
Grid: `display: grid; place-items: center` is a two-line solution.
Absolute: parent `position: relative`, child `top: 50%; left: 50%` then `transform: translate(-50%, -50%)`.

title: Responsive Card Grid
statement: Six cards are inside a `.grid` container. Make a **responsive grid** without media queries: cards should be at least 160px wide, fill the available width equally and wrap to new rows as the window gets narrower. Use a 16px gap.

starter.html:
1
2
3
4
5
6

solution.html:
1
2
3
4
5
6

solutionExplanation: `repeat(auto-fit, minmax(160px, 1fr))` lets the browser create as many columns of at least 160px as fit; `1fr` distributes the remaining space. No media query is needed.
hints: Use `display: grid` on `.grid`.
`grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(160px, 1fr))` does the job.
Use `gap` for spacing between cards.

title: Flexbox Navbar
statement: Build a horizontal navigation bar with flexbox: the logo sits on the **left**, the links (Home, About, Contact) on the **right**, everything vertically centered, with 16px padding and a dark background. Links must have no bullets and a hover colour change.

MySite
  • Home
  • About
  • Contact
starter.css:
body { margin: 0; font-family: sans-serif; }
/* TODO: style .navbar, .logo, .links and the links */

solution.html:
MySite
  • Home
  • About
  • Contact

solutionExplanation: `justify-content: space-between` pushes the logo and link list to opposite ends; the inner `ul` is another flex row. `align-items: center` gives vertical centering.
hints: Make the `nav` a flex container with `align-items: center`.
Put `margin-left: auto` on the `ul` (or use `justify-content: space-between`).
Make the `ul` itself a flex container with a gap and `list-style: none`.

title: Pure CSS Accordion
statement: Make each FAQ item open and close **without JavaScript**. Clicking the question label toggles the answer. Use the hidden checkbox technique: a checkbox, its label and the answer, where `input:checked + label + .answer` shows the answer. Animate the open/close with a `max-height` transition.

starter.html:
Cascading Style Sheets describe how HTML is displayed.

The :checked pseudo-class is enough for simple toggles.

solution.html:
Cascading Style Sheets describe how HTML is displayed.

The :checked pseudo-class is enough for simple toggles.

solutionExplanation: A label toggles its checkbox; the general sibling selector `~` lets CSS react to `:checked`. Because `height: auto` cannot be animated, a generous `max-height` is transitioned instead. For production, the native `<details>` element is the better choice.
hints: Hide the checkbox (`display: none`) - the label still toggles it.
The answer starts with `max-height: 0; overflow: hidden`.
Use the sibling combinator: `.toggle:checked ~ .answer { max-height: 120px }`.

title: CSS Loading Spinner
statement: Create a **40px circular spinner**: a light grey ring where one quarter of the border is coloured, rotating endlessly (1 second per turn, linear). Style the `.spinner` element and define a `@keyframes` animation.

starter.css:
body { display: grid; place-items: center; height: 100vh; margin: 0; }
/* TODO: style .spinner and add @keyframes spin */

solutionExplanation: The ring is a bordered circle; only one side is coloured so rotation is visible. The animation rotates the element a full turn; `linear` keeps a constant speed and `infinite` loops forever.
hints: A circle is a square with `border-radius: 50%`.
Give the border a colour on one side only (`border-top-color`).
Animate `transform: rotate(360deg)` with `animation: spin 1s linear infinite`.

title: Hover Tooltip
statement: Add a tooltip to every element with a `data-tip` attribute: on **hover** (or keyboard focus) a small dark bubble with the tip text appears **above** the element, centered. Use `::after` with `content: attr(data-tip)` - no JavaScript, no extra HTML.
solutionExplanation: `attr()` reads the attribute into generated content. Opacity + a transition gives a fade; `pointer-events: none` stops the bubble from stealing hover.
hints: The host element needs `position: relative`.
`::after` is absolutely positioned: `bottom: 100%; left: 50%; transform: translateX(-50%)`.
Hide it with `opacity: 0` and show it on `:hover` and `:focus`.

title: Counter Component
statement: Build a counter: a number display with id `count` (starts at 0) and three buttons with ids `inc`, `dec` and `reset`. Increment, decrement and reset the number when clicked. Colour the number **green** when positive, **red** when negative and grey at zero.
solutionExplanation: State lives in a variable; every handler changes it and calls one `render()` function that syncs the DOM. This "state -> render" pattern is what frameworks automate.
hints: Keep the value in a variable and write a `render()` function.
Use `addEventListener("click", ...)` for each button.
Set `element.style.color` inside `render`.

title: DOM Todo List
statement:
Build a todo list with plain JavaScript.

* Text input `#todo-input`, button `#add-btn`, list `#todo-list`.
* Clicking **Add** (or pressing Enter) appends a `li` with the text; empty or whitespace-only input is ignored; the input is cleared afterwards.
* Clicking the text of an item toggles a `done` class (line-through).
* Each item has a **Delete** button (`.delete`) that removes it.

starter.js: // TODO: add, toggle and delete todos

solutionExplanation: One listener on the list handles all current and future items (**event delegation**). `closest("li")` finds the item from any click inside it. Using `textContent` avoids HTML injection.
hints: Create elements with `document.createElement("li")`.
Use **event delegation**: one click listener on the `ul` and check `event.target`.
Use `textContent` instead of `innerHTML` for user text.

title: Tabs Component
statement: Make the three tab buttons switch panels. Each `.tab-btn` has a `data-tab` value that matches the `id` of a `.panel`. Clicking a button shows only its panel (add class `active` to the panel and the button, remove it from the others). The first tab is active at start. Panels without `.active` are hidden.

starter.html:
HTML gives structure.
CSS gives style.
JS gives behaviour.

solution.html:
HTML gives structure.
CSS gives style.
JS gives behaviour.

solutionExplanation: Data attributes link buttons to panels without hard-coding IDs in JS. Switching is just removing and adding the `active` class; CSS decides what is visible.
hints: Hide panels with `.panel { display: none }` and show `.panel.active { display: block }`.
Loop over all buttons and add a click listener.
Use `dataset.tab` to read the target id.

title: Modal Dialog
statement:
Build a modal dialog.

* Button `#open-modal` opens the overlay `#overlay` (add class `show`).
* The overlay can be closed by the **X button** (`#close-modal`), by clicking the **dark backdrop** (but not the white box) or by pressing **Escape**.
* The overlay is hidden by default; the white box is centered.

starter.html:
Hello!

This is a modal dialog.
starter.js: // TODO: open and close the modal

solution.html:
Hello!

This is a modal dialog.

solutionExplanation: A fixed full-screen overlay centers the box with flexbox. Clicks inside the box bubble to the overlay, so `e.target === overlay` distinguishes backdrop clicks. A real dialog should also trap focus - the native `<dialog>` element does this for you.
hints: The overlay is `position: fixed; inset: 0` with a semi-transparent background.
To detect a backdrop click compare `event.target === overlay`.
Listen for `keydown` on `document` and check `event.key === "Escape"`.

title: Sign-up Form Validation
statement:
Validate the sign-up form on **submit** (use `novalidate` so the browser does not interfere).

| field | rule |
|---|---|
| `#name` | at least 2 characters |
| `#email` | looks like `something@domain.tld` |
| `#password` | at least 8 characters and contains a digit |
| `#confirm` | equals the password |

* Show the message inside the matching `.error` element and give the invalid input the class `invalid`.
* If all fields are valid show **"Account created!"** in `#success` and clear the form.
* Always call `event.preventDefault()`.
solutionExplanation: Validation is a pure function from values to an errors object, which keeps DOM code simple: render the errors, toggle the `invalid` class, and show success only when the object is empty. Always repeat validation on the server - client checks are only for UX.
hints: Write one small function per rule or a single `validate()` returning an errors object.
A simple email regex: `/^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$/`.
Clear old errors at the start of every submit.
